entries.note: phase 5 leaflet: Draws the map. defer keeps both off the critical path and pr
entries.hunk:
-<!--Draws the map. defer keeps both off the critical path and preserves the order: leaflet.js runs first, so about.js finds window.L and skips its own loader. See the note beside the Leaflet stylesheet in <head>.-->
-<script defer src="../js/leaflet.js"/>
+<!--Loads Leaflet itself and then draws the map. defer keeps it off the critical path; it does not need L on the page beforehand.-->
entries.reason:
PHASE 5 DELIBERATE IMPROVEMENT — the /en/ Leaflet workaround is gone. js/about.js used to resolve 'css/leaflet.css' and 'js/leaflet.js' against the DOCUMENT, so from /en/ they became /en/css/... and 404'd; the English page worked around that by linking Leaflet in <head> itself and loading leaflet.js ahead of about.js. It now resolves both paths against its own script url (document.currentScript, read at top level), so one loader serves the site root and /en/ alike.

Chosen over the migration plan's original wording ('link leaflet.css/js in <head> on both pages') for two measured reasons: that would have put 159kB (14.8kB render-blocking CSS + 144kB JS) on first paint for a section far below the fold, which is exactly the cost the loader exists to avoid; and it would have spread the English page's cascade inversion to the Swedish one — about.js inserts leaflet.css as the FIRST child of <head> on purpose so about.css can override Leaflet's defaults, while the workaround linked it AFTER about.css.

Verified in the browser on both pages after the change: window.L present, #map has class map-live, 12 tiles and 16 markers drawn, leaflet.css resolved to /css/leaflet.css and sitting first in the stylesheet order. The English page's cascade is now correct where it previously was not.

See the comment at the top of js/about.js. The library is vendored from unpkg like every other library in js/ — one less third-party host on the page, and the map keeps working if the CDN does not.
